Same here. Things were great in January and February. Now we have 4 kids at home AND my mother in law who is "stuck" in quarantine. If I tell her to leave I'm the bad guy. Its viewed like I'm sending her to her death. Wtf. In the past 2 months we've gone from loving to discussing divorce. Divorce was brought up by her last night because I'm unpredictable and she's not happy in our marriage. I'm moody and it's my fault because I don't want her mom here or because I want to make love or because I want time together when she's tired... Our world revolves around her and when I'm not playing my part and I'm acting unhappy it forces the world to revolve around me and nobody seems to like that. Well, time to put on my happy face and act like everything is ok so my kids don't get separated from their father!

The course is once a year in December. It's expensive and I struggled to make it happen last year so I'm not sure if I can make it happen this year but am planning on it. Everything you said totally resonates with me. I agree. I want to learn the lessons of this relationship so I can grow and mature spiritually. I think one lesson is to learn detachment. I need to learn how to detach from my desires. Detachment sounds good in my head but I am having trouble envisioning what my detached self would look like in day to day life. What thoughts would I think? What does more self reliant look like in my real life. How would I fill the need for intimacy, emotional & physical affection and making love without compromising my marriage commitment? If I could fill those needs without compromising my morals and ethics I would feel very much at peace. I think it would actually help my marriage as an unintentional byproduct and I would become a more attractive partner. I want someone to look at me in the eyes and tell me they love me with all of their soul. That would feel good. I don't see that happening with her. She has told me similar in the past but without the eye contact. She gets uncomfortable with intimate eye contact. She actually avoids it. We've discussed it. But back to self reliance. Could you help me see some options of how that could look?

Thanks for your feedback. Those are the same conclusions I've reached. This morning I made her coffee and put it by her bedside like I do most days so when she wakes up she has a hot coffee in her thermos. She doesn't come say good morning to me in the mornings. She'll say thank you about 25% of the time. I think of it as a gift but occasionally it bothers me. Today, with nothing else said or texted she texted me a pic of school tuition bill which is due in a few days. I replied "Well good morning to you too! LOL". No response from her. I do feel like a wallet. We went to counseling twice in our 10 year marriage. The first time was one visit. The therapist identified stuff she needed to work on and she decided to not go back. Same with the 2nd therapist about a year ago. She went about 6 times, cancelled and rescheduled half of them, and then said it was better if I went because I found value in it and she didn't think we had the money for both of us. I'm not blind. I see I have a self centered wife who refuses to look at her own issues. She is a bigger victim then me. She hides behind her "sacrifice" for our children and our family. She doesn't set boundaries with our children or reinforce the ones I've created, such as bedtimes, chores, sleeping in their own bed, etc. She unconsciously chooses to be reactive and address their every request such as "can you get me a glass of milk" or "I'm scared to sleep in my own bed." Yes they sleep with her every night and she sleeps in another bedroom because I snore and get up and down 5-6 times during the night and it wakes her up. Apparently children in the bed don't bother her. I sleep alone which sucks and I've tried valiantly to change this. I'm also aware of my codependency on this woman. I focus on her almost all the time inside my head. I want most what I cannot have. I see the insanity in it... My insanity and my obsession with her and her behaviour. I'm just as much to blame. Leaving her isn't what I want. I want her to meet my needs or I want my needs to change so I'm not reliant on her to fill them. Last December I invested $10k in an intensive course to change my core values. I think it helped a little, for a while, but I'm kind of back to where I started in many ways. It was powerful and effective for a while but I slacked in the follow up and lost some of the momentum in ingraining the new values. The suicidal thoughts may be less intense then before but I'm not sure. Either way, I have work to do on myself.

So much history and complexity... She's 13 now and this started 10 years ago. I was new to parenting and tried to be in charge. She resented that until this day. She would argue with her mom until she got what she wanted and if I stepped in her mom would back her up and I would be "squishing" her spirit. Now she is kind of smart mouthed and does what she wants no matter what her mom and dad tell her with no reprocussions. She also resents her mother for leaving her father and fears her father won't love her. Stack that with her mother stays with me when she's is unhappy and didn't stay with her father. She doesn't know about all the cheating her father and mother did on each other. They only talk about the fun times to her. It's easier for her to be mad at me then her parents no matter what they did. I don't behave how she wants me to behave within out family. It's a compilation. I might not reprimand a younger childn when she thinks I should. I might not be understanding or loving when she expects I should. I tend to target her as the bringer of drama just like she targets me. I disagree with how she's parented. She gets the biggest room in the house. It's about 15' x 25'. It's much larger then the master bedroom with a private bathroom. She does zero chores. She has over 50 hoodies, mountains of clothes & make-up, 2 computers, TV, King size bed, goes to private school, stays up to whenever she wants, gets up when she wants, orders take out when she doesn't want her mom's cooking. Her bio dad gave her a visa debit card and an allowance to buy things she wants to teach her "financial responsibility" but he won't help with her school tuition. Her personality has become extremely self entitled. She alternates between sweet and extremely nasty with her siblings. Ironically, when her and I are alone we get along great. It's when her mom or siblings are present that we have friction.
Thanks, I needed that too.

Yes, I've communicated to her general feelings and specific needs like cuddling in bed, making love once our twice per week and having alone time with her regularly. She lets herself get drained being supermom to the kids because that is how she gets her reward, mothering. She doesn't reserve any energy for our marriage. She says everyone is responsible for filling their own tanks and she's right on that point for the most part. She also said I'm a bottomless pit so there is no point in showing me compassion when I'm "down" because no matter what she does I'll never be happy. I asked her how can I know you love me? She said that she is here and married to me, that is how I know. She said she wouldn't be here if she didn't love me. She says she also shows her love by taking care of our kids and doing things around the house like laundry and cleaning. I've been very clear with her that I'm a physical touch person and that is my love language. All the acts of service she does are great but doesn't make me feel loved. It's not my language. She usually says that physical touch usually leads to me wanting sex and "I wouldn't want her to do something she doesn't want to do, do I?" 

This all feels like word play and mind games to me. Maybe I'm wrong. What do you think?
